page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-192 is an accelerator-focused instance within the GPU Machines family, designed for high-throughput graphics workloads and parallel processing. Built on the x86_64 processor architecture, the host provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 720 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by four NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs providing an aggregate of 384 GB of video memory across the cluster. The configuration contains no bundled local storage volumes, requiring external persistent network storage for file systems and dataset retention. Network provisioning includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, reflecting an internal cluster deployment model.

The combination of 384 GB total VRAM and 192 dedicated compute threads prioritizes dense graphical rendering, high-concurrency simulation, and extensive artificial intelligence training or inference pipelines. Because resource allocation scales heavily on both host CPU cores and high-tier enterprise GPUs, the instance represents an intensive hardware tier targeted at enterprise workstation virtualization, visual computing, and large-scale data science operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-192 is a high-density GPU compute instance engineered for graphics processing and parallelized scientific computations. Running on the x86_64 CPU architecture, the server delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 720 GB of system memory, maintaining a 3.75 GB per core memory profile. Accelerated computation is driven by four NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, presenting an aggregate capacity of 384 GB of GDDR VRAM. The system features no integrated local storage drives, requiring administrators to attach network block storage volumes for persistent data needs, and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dense integration of multi-GPU acceleration and extensive host CPU resources makes the platform suitable for distributed machine learning workflows, large-scale 3D rendering pipelines, visual effects generation, and compute-heavy data engineering tasks.
